entries.strand: Mathematics: Developing a sense of number
entries.text: Begin to use ordinal numbers from 1st to at least 3rd in practical contexts, for example, toys or people in a line, running races.

entries.strand: Mathematics: Developing a sense of number
entries.text: Use ordinal numbers from 1st to 10th in practical contexts, for example, to talk about a sequence of events or activities.

entries.strand: Mathematics: Developing a sense of number
entries.text: Recognise and use ordinal numbers from 1st to 10th, for example, 'What is the tiger's position in the line? ... Which toy is in front of the tiger? ... What is its position in the line?'.
Recognise and talk about patterns in the environment.
Copy and create simple repeating patterns of repeating units (e.g. [red, blue]; [red, blue, yellow]; [red, blue, blue]; [red, blue, blue, yellow]) and say what would come next in the pattern.

Use familiar language to describe sequences of items, including identifying errors in patterns of colour, shape or size, for example, 'It goes square, circle, triangle, square, circle, circle ... the last one is wrong, it should be a triangle.'.
Ask for permission before using a digital device.
Ask for help when they encounter problems or unexpected behaviour when using a digital device.
Recognise that digital devices should be used only for short periods of time.
Handle digital devices with care and consideration for others.
Recognise that online content may be available to everyone connected to the internet, so they should tell an adult if any online content makes them feel unsafe or uncomfortable.
